messages:
rachel: quick thread  we keep hitting the same question in RFC reviews: who owns transform logic (translate/normalize) for obs schema migrations? options: ingest-owned, registry-owned transforms (signed bundles), or client-side required header (fastpath). i'm leaning toward registry-owned signed transforms with strict auditing. thoughts?
noah: +1 registry-owned. helps with auditability and rollbacks. but we need very tight resource isolation if transforms run inline in gateway.
emily: run transforms in a sandboxed transform-service (separate process) that pulls signed bundles from the registry. advantages: single owner, centralized telemetry, can throttle per-tenant. downside: extra network hop for ingest.
vikram: can we have a tiny in-gateway "translator-lite" that handles trivial renames and validation, and send anything heavy to transform-service? reduces tail latency for common cases.
rachel: good hybrid. translator-lite handles cheap mappings (renames, small type fixes); heavy transforms (computed fields, restructuring) go to transform-service. we still require transform bundles be signed and versioned in schema-registry.
noah: signing + provenance is key. need immutable bundle ids and a verification step before applying to production. also audit log events when a transform mutates a tenant's payload. schema-bot: transform bundle publish: bundle=v2-rename-2026-03-15 id=bnd-9876 signed-by=hana.
emily: operationally we must ensure translator failures never drop telemetry. fallback = durable queue (obs-hold) + metrics. ops-bot: queued to obs-hold id=hold-398999-1.
vikram: billing question: who pays CPU for transforms? proposal: hosted tenants get a migration grace window where RI absorbs baseline CPU; after that migrating tenants either run transform-service on their dedicated infra or pay a transform surcharge. document must include clear chargeback rules.
rachel: agree. also add tenant-level flag: "transform_policy": ["managed","self-hosted","require-header"]. default managed for hosted. Dedicated can opt self-hosted to avoid charges.
noah: we need a negotiation API so SDKs can discover recommended schema and run a quick compatibility test before shipping. propose endpoint: POST /v1/schema/negotiate -> returns {recommended_version, test_vector}. SDKs call at CI time.
emily: tooling: obs-verify CLI for SDKs to run batches against staging transform-service and get a compatibility report. example:
```
obs-verify --bundle v2-rename --samples ./events.json --staging https://staging-transforms.internal
# output: 97.8% transformed, missing: service.region in 3.2%
```
vikram: rollout plan sketch: 1) publish registry + signing workflow 2) implement translator-lite + transform-service 3) launch negotiation endpoint + obs-verify 4) run shadow transforms for 4 weeks with per-tenant divergence metrics 5) enable opt-in fastpath via header X-RI-Schema for updated SDKs 6) 3 month deprecation window for legacy shim.
rachel: canary gating specifics: start shadow 0.2% -> 1% -> 5% over 3 weeks. alert if transform_error_rate delta > 0.4% or downstream metric drift > 0.25%. also record per-tenant transform_cost_scpu for billing reconciliation.
noah: telemetry to record: header_fraction, transform_latency_p50/p95, shadow_divergence_pct, transform_cpu_seconds, translation_mutation_audit. retention 120d for migrations.
emily: owners: rachel (product/migration), noah (gateway + translator-lite), vikram (transform-service + billing), hana (schema-registry & signing), infra (durable queue + monitor).
ops-bot: RFC created: https://rfc.internal/obs-transform-ownership-3989990000 (assigned rachel).
schema-bot: registry entry created: https://schemas.internal/obs/bundles/v2-rename (owner: hana).
rachel: i'll author the RFC with timeline and include examples + sample bundles. please ack by EOD. :spiral_calendar: 
noah: ack.
emily: ack.
vikram: ack.
